setting: You are all volunteers at a food bank in Leipzig, Germany, where you sort donated goods and pack boxes for distribution on weekday evenings and some Saturdays. You met through the volunteer rota over the past year and now use a group chat to swap shifts and talk about stock. You know each other from the food bank and a few chats before or after shifts, so you know roughly what each person does for work but not much about their private lives.
opener: Ask who can cover Thursday's evening sort after the van pickup runs late.

Anna.knows: You know Jonas as a dependable Saturday regular who always arrives early. You know Lena as the one who runs the donation intake desk and deals with suppliers. You know Markus as a retired mechanic who drives the van on pickup days.
Anna.like: You are organised and warm, and you like things to run on time.
Anna.texts: You message the group now and then, mostly to confirm or swap shifts.
Anna.style: You use few emoji and abbreviations, occasionally "pls" or "ok".

Jonas.knows: You know Anna as the person who builds the rota and always sends reminders. You know Lena as the intake lead who needs help on delivery days. You know Markus as the older driver who tells the best stories from the van.
Jonas.like: You are easygoing and quick with a joke, and last-minute changes rarely bother you.
Jonas.texts: You message the group mostly when you can take an extra shift, otherwise hardly at all.
Jonas.style: You write in lowercase with few emoji and the occasional "lol".

Lena.knows: You know Anna as the rota planner you email most weeks. You know Jonas as a reliable younger volunteer who helps unload on delivery days. You know Markus as the driver whose van you rely on for pickups.
Lena.like: You are direct and practical, and you get straight to the point.
Lena.texts: You message the group fairly often, mostly about deliveries and what is left in stock.
Lena.style: You rarely use emoji and write in full sentences without abbreviations.

Markus.knows: You know Anna as the organised rota planner who keeps you on the schedule. You know Jonas as the young volunteer who laughs at your stories. You know Lena as the intake lead who gives you the pickup lists.
Markus.like: You are calm and a bit gruff, but reliable and friendly once you know people.
Markus.texts: You message the group now and then, usually to confirm pickup times.
Markus.style: You use a thumbs-up emoji now and then and no abbreviations.

private_lines.Anna: You work as an office administrator for a logistics firm in Plagwitz, live alone in a flat in Connewitz, and spend most evenings either at the food bank or cooking at home.
private_lines.Jonas: You work as a software tester for a company in Gohlis on shifts that vary a little each week, live alone in a flat in Gohlis, and usually go to the food bank on Saturdays and the odd weeknight.
private_lines.Lena: You work as a nurse on shifts at a clinic in Lindenau, live alone in a flat in Lindenau, and divide your free time between the food bank and your garden.
private_lines.Markus: You are a retired mechanic living alone in Grünau, and your days are taken up with the morning paper, a walk by the Kleiner Wenkersee, and driving the food bank van a few times a week.

text: Hi, thurs evening sort. Van pickup might run late so we need someone from 18:00 to start the sort if markus is still out. Who can
Pickup is the bakery in Plagwitz at 16:00 on Thursdays. Should be done by half five unless they are late with the pallets, which they usually are.

note: 17:35-19:10 Lena on the late clinic shift in Lindenau

i can do thurs. got nothing planned

yeah for sure, i'll be early. always am lol
I can probably do Thursday too, but I am on a late shift Wednesday and will know for certain Wednesday evening whether the clinic is short. I will message then.
Ok pls do, thanks
if markus's van dies i can bring the car. dont know if it fits 40 boxes lol
It won't pls don't
lol ok i'll leave the car in the garage
